### Known gaps

- Storage RP account state (StorageProvider.accounts) does not survive a snapshot/restore cycle -- only InMemoryBackend's resource-group/generic-resource/provider-registration state is persisted (see ops.StorageAccountCRUD). Fix is additive: give StorageProvider its own Snapshot/Restore and wire it into Handler.Snapshot/Restore alongside the backend's.
- ServiceBus RP state (ServiceBusProvider's namespaces/queues/topics/subscriptions maps) does not survive a snapshot/restore cycle either, the same known gap as StorageAccountCRUD above and for the same reason -- no ResourceProvider's own state is currently wired into Handler.Snapshot/Restore.
- TestTerraform_Azure_ServiceBus (M9) could not be confirmed against a live tofu apply on this milestone's local macOS development sandbox, due to the same pre-existing host-OS-specific TLS-trust gap documented for M7/M8 (AZURE.md section 10.10) -- apply fails at ARM's own metadata-discovery call, before reaching any ServiceBus-specific code. Compensating verification: test/integration/azurearm_test.go's TestIntegration_AzureARM_ServiceBusLifecycleAndCrossServiceWiring exercises the identical ARM CRUD + cross-service-wiring path over plain HTTP and passed; wire-shape questions were answered by reading the pinned terraform-provider-azurerm/go-azure-sdk source directly. Should be re-confirmed against a green CI run (expected to work on Linux).
- Token endpoint accepts any (or a missing) client_id/grant_type without validation and always issues a token; a malformed client_credentials request should arguably 400 with invalid_request/unsupported_grant_type per RFC 6749, matching AAD's own error shape more closely.
- Direct-data-plane storage resources (azurerm_storage_container/_blob/_queue/_table) are covered as of M8 via the new services/azurestoragevhost virtual-hosted-style listener (AZURE.md section 10.8 finding (9)); azurerm_storage_share (File Share) remains out of scope -- no gopherstack file-share service exists.
- Multi-account namespace isolation: all ARM-created storage accounts alias one shared Blob/Queue/Table container/queue/table namespace (services/azureblob/azurequeue/azuretable discard the account-name path segment entirely). Two ARM storage accounts see each other's containers. Deferred to M10 per AZURE.md section 10.4's original note; StorageAccounts.RegisterAccount/DeleteAccount (interfaces.go) is the forward-compat seam for that fix.
- ARM error codes are a small hand-picked table (errors.go's errorDetails), not audited against ARM's full published error-code catalog the way services/sqs's errorDetails table has been over multiple audit passes.
- management locks, Azure Policy, RBAC/Microsoft.Authorization, ARM template deployments (Microsoft.Resources/deployments), PATCH-merge semantics beyond full-replace, $filter/$expand and nextLink pagination on list operations, cross-subscription/cross-tenant, resource moves, What-If, and LRO polling are all explicitly out of MVP scope per AZURE.md section 10.1/10.3 -- not bugs, deliberate scope boundaries for this milestone.
- Flexible servers: only the listed operations are modelled. PostgreSQL administrators (Entra), backups, migrations, virtual-network subnet usage, and MySQL updateConfigurations (batch), maintenances, logFiles, backupAndExport, advanced threat protection, Entra administrators, failover, detachVNet, resetGtid and private endpoint connections answer from the generic store or 404.
- Flexible servers: replicas and point-in-time/geo restores are state-level (a copy of the source configuration and database list); under the docker engine they are refused with 400 InvalidParameterValue because a new container would start without the source data or the administrator password. Replication is not run.
- Flexible servers: server parameter changes are stored, validated against a documented subset of parameters and flagged pending-restart, but are not applied to the docker engine; max_connections defaults follow the documented per-SKU tables for both engines, but the docker engine itself is not started with that value; the PostgreSQL max_connections range, every other parameter default/range/allowed value, and the MySQL storage IOPS formula (360 minimum, 3 per GiB) are not taken from a published table.
- Flexible servers: firewall rules (including the 0.0.0.0 allow-Azure-services rule) are stored and validated but not enforced - the docker engine listens on loopback only; engines are not relaunched after a gopherstack restart or snapshot restore; the automatic restart of a stopped server (7 days for PostgreSQL, 30 days for MySQL per the Learn how-to pages), maintenance windows, HA failover, data encryption and Entra authentication are stored but not acted on.
- Flexible servers: error codes and HTTP statuses outside stop/restart are unverified (no primary source documents them): name collision (409 Conflict), write during a pending operation, write to a stopped server, validation failures (400 InvalidParameterValue), and failed operations (InternalServerError). The busy-code spelling (SeverBusyWithOtherOperation vs ServerBusyWithOtherOperation) is documented one way and observed another.
- Flexible servers: not modelled although documented - PostgreSQL Premium SSD v2 (storage up to 64 TiB in 1 GiB steps, terraform storage_type PremiumV2_LRS), PostgreSQL confidential-compute SKUs (terraform regex Standard_*C*ads_v5), PostgreSQL E6ds_v4, the PostgreSQL rule that a private DNS zone name must differ from the server name, MySQL storage IOPS pre-provisioning limits below the SKU maximum, and MySQL B1s IOPS (not published).
- Flexible servers: no Terraform azurerm fixture (azurerm_postgresql_flexible_server, azurerm_mysql_flexible_server) yet; the SDK-driven tests are the only wire proof.
- AKS: snapshots, machines, managedNamespaces, identityBindings, private endpoint connections, rotateServiceAccountSigningKeys and the agent pool abort are not modelled (the generic store keeps what is PUT).
- AKS: node pools are metadata; no VMs back them and the k3s engine runs one server node regardless of pool counts.
- AKS runCommand: with the engine the command runs in the k3s node (not in a pod) through /bin/sh with KUBECONFIG pointed at the node's own admin kubeconfig; kubectl is the k3s one, helm is not in the k3s image so helm commands exit 127; clusterToken is ignored; the context zip travels in an environment variable, so it is limited to 96 KiB of base64; logs are capped at 1 MiB and a command at 10 minutes (both unverified limits). Without the engine no node can schedule the command pod, so the command ends provisioningState failed with the reason Learn documents for that case (troubleshoot/azure/azure-kubernetes/resolve-az-aks-command-invoke-failures, Cause 1: KubernetesPerformanceError, 'Failed to run command due to cluster perf issue, container command-<ID> in aks-command namespace did not start within 30s on your cluster...', with <ID> the 32-hex command id); how the service places the code relative to the message in the result body, and whether it instead answers 404 Not Found as the same page's symptom table says, is unverified. Command results are kept per cluster (the newest 50) and a restored snapshot fails the ones that were running.
- AKS abort: only operations the emulator runs for a while can be aborted - creating or updating a cluster with the engine on, start, and certificate rotation; the abort answers 202 after the operation has wound down, and 409 OperationNotAllowed when nothing runs (the 409 is documented, the code string is not). A cancelled create leaves the cluster in provisioningState Canceled without a node until the next PUT or start. Agent pool abort is not routed.
- AKS rotateClusterCertificates: with the engine five fresh CAs (server, client, request-header, etcd peer and server) are generated, staged in the node and installed with k3s certificate rotate-ca --force (docs.k3s.io/cli/certificate: a new self-signed root needs --force), then the node is restarted and reissues every certificate under them, so listClusterUserCredential/AdminCredential return the new CA and the old one no longer verifies the API server (Learn azure/aks/certificate-rotation: rotating the cluster CA refreshes API server, kubelet and service account certificates; the real service also recreates nodes, up to 30 minutes of downtime). The static admin token is not rotated and pods are not restarted to trust the new root; without the engine the emulated CA and token are replaced, so kubeconfigs fetched earlier stop matching. The failure code ClusterCertificateRotationFailed is not from a primary source.
- AKS resetAADProfile / resetServicePrincipalProfile: both exist in 2026-08-01 (resetAADProfile carries the deprecation warning in its description) and are accepted for every supported api-version. The profile is stored (serverAppSecret and the service principal secret are write-only); the refusals for an AKS-managed AAD cluster and for a cluster without a service principal (the spec says the latter is not allowed) use OperationNotAllowed, which is not from a primary source. No legacy AAD token validation happens.
- AKS maintenanceConfigurations: validated against the 2026-08-01 schema (required durationHours 4-24, startTime, exactly one schedule type with the documented interval ranges, utcOffset and date formats, notAllowedDates/notAllowedTime ordering) and the Learn table of schedule types per name (default weekly only; aksManagedAutoUpgradeSchedule and aksManagedNodeOSUpgradeSchedule all four); the 400 code InvalidParameter, the rule that default needs a window or timeInWeek, that the aksManaged names refuse timeInWeek/notAllowedTime, and the utcOffset hour limit (14) are not from a primary source. Windows are stored and returned but never gate an upgrade; list is not paged.
- AKS trustedAccessRoleBindings / trustedAccessRoles: bindings are stored with the 24-character name rule, at most 8 per cluster (Learn) and the rule that each role is <source resource type>/<role> of the source resource's type; role names are not checked against a catalog and no ClusterRoleBinding is created in the node. The role catalog lists only the roles whose rules the API reference publishes (Microsoft.MachineLearningServices/workspaces reader); writer, mlworkload, backup-operator and the other documented roles are missing because their rules are not published. Error codes are unverified.
- AKS engine state: the k3s data directory lives on a named volume (gopherstack-aks-<hash>), the node name is pinned and the join token is derived from the cluster, so stop/start, a snapshot restore and a restart with persistence on all resume the same cluster state; a running node left by a crashed gopherstack is adopted by resource label (the data volume of a cluster that no longer exists is removed at restore). Without persistence a restart forgets the cluster, and creating a cluster of the same name discards the leftover volume. Runtimes that cannot keep stopped containers or create volumes keep state only while the container lives.
- AKS: addon profiles, AAD, auto-upgrade, http proxy, security and storage profiles are stored and returned but not interpreted; the VM catalog and Kubernetes patch versions are representative subsets; the kubeconfig carries a bearer token only (no client certificates).
- Container Apps: init containers, subPath mounts, NfsAzureFile volumes, additional TCP ports, exposedPort/TCP transport routing, session affinity, CORS, ipSecurityRestrictions enforcement, custom domains, Dapr runtime, probes and managed-identity registry pulls are stored but not run or enforced.
- Container Apps: KEDA scale rules other than the http/tcp concurrency settings (queue, custom) are stored but never scale replicas; scale-out is driven by in-flight requests through the ingress.
- Container Apps jobs: Schedule and Event triggers are stored and validated but never fire (only start runs an execution); replicaRetryLimit and replicaTimeout are not enforced.
- Container Apps: restored revisions have no replicas until their first request (or a restart), even with minReplicas above 0.

- Container Instances: interactive exec and attach need a websocket terminal session; both answer 501 NotImplemented.
- Container Instances: not supported and rejected with 400 InvalidRequestContent: Windows containers, gitRepo volumes, GPUs, liveness/readiness probes, init containers, zones, subnet and DNS configuration, diagnostics, confidential/dedicated SKUs, spot priority, encryption, extensions, UDP ports.

### Deferred

- M7 initial implementation. No prior audit passes to report.
- M9 added the Microsoft.ServiceBus RP (ServiceBusNamespaceCRUD/ServiceBusQueueTopicSubscriptionCRUD/ServiceBusAuthorizationRuleListKeys). QC pass over the pre-existing implementation found and fixed two real bugs before any Terraform run (List not filtering by resource group for queues/topics/subscriptions; DeleteResourcesInGroup's cascade delete never matching due to a double-pipe key-prefix bug) -- see AZURE.md section 10.10's M9 entry for full detail.
- M9's first real-CI run (PR #2466, terraform-tests (6) job on Linux, past the macOS TLS-trust gap) surfaced a third real bug: classifyServiceBusPath had no case for namespaces/{ns}/networkRuleSets/default, which terraform-provider-azurerm's namespace Read calls unconditionally on every namespace regardless of SKU or config -- see ops.ServiceBusNamespaceNetworkRuleSet above and AZURE.md section 10.10's M9 entry for full detail. Checked queue/topic/subscription/authorizationRule Read functions in the same pinned source for the same class of unconditional sub-resource probe; none exists (each Read function only calls its own client.Get).
